column1: Preheat the oven to 248°F (120°C) using top and bottom heat.
In a clean glass or steel bowl, slowly whip the egg whites with the salt until foamy, then increase speed until the bubbles are small and even.
Once stiff peaks form, add the sugar gradually and whip until glossy and the sugar has dissolved without overbeating.
Sift in the cornstarch, add the vinegar, and gently fold together with a spatula.
Draw a 24–26 cm circle on parchment on a baking sheet and spread the meringue inside it about 2.5 cm tall.
Bake on the lowest rack about 1 1/2 hours until crisp outside, then turn off the oven and let it cool inside with the door ajar, ideally overnight.
For the custard, put the egg yolks, milk, sugar, cornstarch, and snipped gelatin sheets in a saucepan.
Heat while stirring until it thickens to a thick custard, moving the pan off the heat briefly if it thickens too fast.
Transfer to a bowl, cover the surface with plastic wrap, and chill completely, then whisk until smooth.
Whip the cream to stiff peaks and fold it into the custard.
Just before serving, place the meringue on a platter, spread with the cream, and top with the fresh berries.
